steps.question: Which states get their own visible value?
steps.why: Pressed gets its own value for touch.

steps.rule: The fill of the item the pointer or the keyboard is on, or whose submenu is open. A state shows on the item's background, one step from the surface it sits on: darker in light, lighter in dark.
steps.pick: neutral.100, two steps darker than the surfaces it sits on (neutral.0), so the item under the pointer or the keyboard reads as a band without lifting off the page. It skips neutral.50, the page canvas, so a menu item never matches the page behind it.
steps.darkPick: neutral.100, one step lighter than the surfaces it sits on (neutral.50), so the item under the pointer or the keyboard reads as a band on the menu and on cards.

steps.why: The dimmed page focuses the reader on the dialog.

steps.pick: neutral.0, the same as content (surface.default): a menu stands out by its edge and its one shadow, not by its fill.
steps.darkPick: neutral.50, the same as content (surface.default): a menu stands out by its edge and its one shadow, not by its fill, as in light.

steps.rule: Quiet edges and dividers. Decorative, so it has no contrast minimum.
steps.pick: neutral.200: a quiet line that stays visible on every surface it meets (lowest 1.33:1, on surface.canvas). It decorates, so it holds no contrast minimum.
steps.darkPick: neutral.200: a quiet line that stays visible on every surface it meets (lowest 1.76:1, on surface.default). It decorates, so it holds no contrast minimum.

steps.pick: radius.12: We use a 12px corner for article cards, menus and dialogs in order to make each card read as a separate object, in a warm tone by brand convention. A larger radius does this by breaking the outline with a curve wider than the 8px controls inside it. So a card reads as one calm object on the page, because containers get their own corner (shape.roles, shape.count) and the brand is warm (brand.q1).

shadow.overlay: We use step 2 of the shadow scale for menus and dialogs in order to show their height as floating layers. The cast shade does this by a 12px offset and a 32px blur in a 16% warm brown. So a menu lifts off warm paper without a hard edge, because only what floats rises (elevation.roles) and shadows are soft (elevation.values).
steps.darkPick: shadow.overlay-dark: We use the light shadow's shape for menus and dialogs in dark in order to show the same floating height by the dark-shade relation. The cast shade does this by the same 12px offset and 32px blur, at 50% black instead of 16% brown. So a menu still lifts off the dark page, though its shade reads weaker on dark than in light, because only what floats rises (elevation.roles) and dark ships for night reading (theming.values).

radius.8: We use an 8px corner for menu options in order to keep nesting by the relation: the 12px surface corner minus the panel's 4px padding. The inner radius does this by following the outer curve at the padding's distance. So an option's curve runs parallel to its menu's curve, because surfaces take 12px (shape.roles, brand.q1) and the panel's padding is 4px (spacing.values).

steps.question: Which color roles does it need?
How many signals carry each meaning?
steps.why: Status is rare; color and a word are enough.
A tint shows the choice clearly on warm paper.

steps.rule: The fill of a selected or current item, or a toggle that is on.
steps.pick: navy.light.100: a tint of the brand, 1.22:1 from content, always beside its edge (border.selected), so selection is never color alone.
steps.darkPick: navy.dark.100: a tint of the brand, 1.2:1 from content, always beside its edge (border.selected), so selection is never color alone.

steps.rule: The edge that marks a selected item, beside its fill, so selection is never color alone.
steps.pick: navy.light.600: the edge beside a selected fill, so selection is never color alone, 11.5:1 on surface.default, above the 3:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: navy.dark.600: the edge beside a selected fill, so selection is never color alone, 6.86:1 on surface.default, above the 3:1 floor.
